title: Co-reading explainer gallery — audited interactive figures of what a language model writes when asked to reason about a geometric configuration
description:
A gallery of co-reading explainers: interactive isometric figures (also anywidgets for Jupyter / marimo), 1920×1080 stills, two-voice scripts and ledgers of what can and cannot be said, each built only from the frozen outputs of a pre-registered line of measurements whose cards (PREREG = the frozen promise written before the run, RESULT = the read-out written after it, corrections appended and never edited in) are included verbatim in Japanese with an English index. Every number on a page is anchored to the data by a checker with a positive control (check_claims.py); the question texts are traced to the public ConstructGap suite (v1.0.1) with an md5 at every stage; station 1 was judged under seal by readers from a different model family than its maker; stations 2 and 3 were each built by two makers in parallel, read under an acceptance form whose main condition is whether the next step can be seen, and received as one version made from the readers' choices and an audit.

Co-reading is a prototype for people reading together what an AI has generated, in course material as well as in research with AI. The most important acceptance condition is whether the next step can be seen; two makers are there to find the variation, and the received version is made by weighing their difference, not by picking a winner.

The gallery is read as one line of three stations: moy-2 (from algebraic analysis to elementary geometry — a reflection formula offered to OLMo-3 32B base as a tool; what it computes and what it writes in its proof field), moy-1 (elementary geometry — OLMo-3 32B on a two-circle problem asked open, and with one sentence that blocks the easy answer) and moy-5 (how to make a model draw the auxiliary line — where the apex, a mean proportional, appears when frontier models answer a parabola problem; the board drawn as a section of a cone with its cutting plane). This release contains all three stations: moy-2 (entry v1.3), moy-1 (received version v3.1) and moy-5 (received version v2.3.1).

View the figures on GitHub Pages: https://moyhig-ecs.github.io/coread-explainer-gallery/ (the hash in a page URL is the state; #s19 is the ledger). Run them from this archive: unzip, open <entry>/dist/<page>.html (the pages are self-contained) or serve the folder with python3 -m http.server. Zenodo does not render HTML.

Made with the coread-explainer skill for Claude Code on the Anatomy kit (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Ryan). Gallery: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Manabu Higashida; the quoted model outputs are data.
